info.title: Hostinger Mail API
info.description:
# Overview The Hostinger Mail API provides a set of endpoints that allow developers to manage Hostinger Email programmatically. This API enables you to manage mailboxes and related resources tied to your Hostinger account. The API is (mostly) RESTful and uses standard HTTP methods and status codes. # Official SDKs Integrate the Hostinger Mail API in minutes using official, idiomatic SDKs - no more hand-rolling HTTP calls. Published to native package managers, so it's a one-line install. - **PHP** - `composer require hostinger/mail-api-php-sdk` ([GitHub](https://github.com/hostinger/mail-api-php-sdk)) - **TypeScript / Node.js** - `npm install hostinger-mail-api-sdk` ([GitHub](https://github.com/hostinger/mail-api-typescript-sdk)) - **Python** - `pip install hostinger-mail-api` ([GitHub](https://github.com/hostinger/mail-api-python-sdk)) - **CLI** - `brew install hostinger/tap/hostinger-mail` ([GitHub](https://github.com/hostinger/mail-api-cli)) # AI agents (MCP) Want to read or send your email from Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or any other AI assistant? Hostinger ships an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that wraps this API: ``` https://mcp.mail.hostinger.com/mcp ``` Use the same API token from the Hostinger Panel. Your agent only reaches what the token permits — order-scoped, optionally restricted to specific mailboxes within the order.
Claude Code (CLI) ```bash claude mcp add --scope user --transport http \ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN" \ -- hostinger-email https://mcp.mail.hostinger.com/mcp ```
Claude Desktop Claude Desktop connects to MCP servers via stdio. Use the `mcp-remote` bridge to talk to our HTTP server. Requires Node.js (`npx` ships with it). Edit the Claude Desktop config file. Path depends on your OS: - **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` - **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` - **Linux:** `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` Set the contents to: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hostinger-email": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.mail.hostinger.com/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN" ] } } } ``` Quit Claude Desktop fully (not just close the window) and reopen it. The connector icon should appear in the message composer. If you have Claude Desktop's paid "Custom Connectors" feature, you can skip the `mcp-remote` bridge entirely and add the HTTP URL directly via the in-app UI: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hostinger-email": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.mail.hostinger.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN" } } } } ```
Cursor Create or edit `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global) or `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project root: ```json { "mcpServers": { "hostinger-email": { "url": "https://mcp.mail.hostinger.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN" } } } } ``` Restart Cursor. The server is also configurable via `Cmd-Shift-P` → `View: Open MCP Settings` (newer Cursor versions).
What can the agent do? Same as this REST API - read, search, send, move, flag, delete messages; list folders and mailboxes; manage webhooks; manage calendars and calendar events. The agent calls these endpoints under the hood using your API token. The agent only reaches what your token permits. Tokens are scoped to a single Hostinger order, and you can further restrict each token to specific mailboxes within that order when generating it in the Panel.
# Other plugins - **ChatGPT plugin** - read and send your Hostinger email straight from ChatGPT ([Open](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a323a8a890c819190480c9044395170)) # Feedback from integrations and AI agents Something did not work, was slow, or is missing? Tell the Hostinger mail team directly from your code or your agent: `POST /api/v1/mailboxes/{mailboxResourceId}/feedback` (MCP tool `email_report_feedback`) with a `score` (1-10) and a short `message`. Reports reach the team's feedback channel within minutes. Report when a call returned `4xx`/`5xx` or unexpected data, when a response was too slow, when documentation was missing or unclear, or when a capability you needed does not exist. Mention the failing operation and the status code you received so the team can find the request. Never include tokens, passwords or email contents: messages are scrubbed of secrets and capped at 2000 characters. Send one report per distinct issue. # Authentication The API uses tokens for authentication. To authenticate your requests, you need to include a valid bearer token in the `Authorization` header of your HTTP requests: ```yaml Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN ``` API tokens can be created and managed from the email provisioning tab in the Hostinger Panel. Tokens are scoped to a single order; their permissions are limited to that order. Only mailboxes belonging to the order can be accessed and managed by an API token. # Rate Limiting To ensure fair usage and prevent abuse, the API enforces rate limits on the number of requests that can be made within a certain time period. If you exceed the rate limit, you will receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Your IP address might get temporarily blocked if you exceed the rate limit multiple times. # Calendar Calendar endpoints manage the calendars of a mailbox and the events in them. They are available only when the mailbox plan includes the calendar; otherwise they return `403` with code `ERR_PAYWALL`. Events are identified by a calendar `uuid` and an event `uuid`. Every occurrence of a recurring event shares the event `uuid`; `recurrenceId` picks one occurrence, and `scope` (`this`, `future`, `all`) says how much of the series a change applies to. Changes to an event with attendees send invitation, update or cancellation emails; answering an invitation emails the organizer. Pass `notifyAttendees` as `false` on an update, reschedule or delete to skip them. Event writes accept an optional `If-Match` header holding the `etag` of the event. When the event changed since that `etag` was read, the request fails with `412` and code `ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED` instead of overwriting the newer version. The list of events is not paginated: it returns the events overlapping a time range of at most 32 days, with `meta.truncated` telling whether some were left out. # Parameters All requests sent to the API must have the content type `application/json`. `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` methods may include a JSON object in the request body. Documentation provides the required structure and examples of the object. Some endpoints require path parameters. These parameters are included in the URL path and are marked with curly braces. # Response envelope All non-`204` responses wrap the payload in a top-level `data` field. Single resource: ```json { "data": { "resourceId": "AC1a2b3c4d5e6f7g", "address": "user@example.com" } } ``` Collection (empty or otherwise): ```json { "data": [] } ``` # Pagination Paginated responses include a top-level `pagination` object alongside `data`. By default, the API returns 50 items per page. The page number can be specified using the `page` query parameter, for example: `/core/v1/public/mailboxes?page=2`. ```json { "data": [], "pagination": { "page": 1, "perPage": 25, "total": 137, "totalPages": 6 } } ``` # Errors All `4xx` and `5xx` responses share a single envelope. Always parse `code` for programmatic handling; `error` is a human-readable message intended for logs and support tickets. ```json { "error": "Mailbox not found.", "code": "ERR_MAILBOX_NOT_FOUND", "params": {} } ```

post.description:
Create an event in one calendar of the mailbox. `calendarUuid` comes from `listCalendars`: use the calendar with `default` true unless another one is named. A calendar the mailbox can only read is rejected with `403` and code `ERR_EVENT_NOT_EDITABLE`.
The mailbox becomes the organizer and every address in `attendees` immediately receives an email invitation, which cannot be recalled. Without attendees no email is sent.
A timed event needs `allDay` false, `start`, `end` and `timeZone`. An all-day event needs `allDay` true and a `start` date; `end` is optional. Set `recurrenceRule` for a repeating event and `reminder` for an alarm.
Returns the created event. Its `uuid` is the `eventUuid` for `getCalendarEvent`, `updateCalendarEvent`, `rescheduleCalendarEvent` and `deleteCalendarEvent`.

parameters.name: mailboxResourceId
parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the bearer token is authorized for.

parameters.name: calendarUuid
parameters.description: Calendar identifier: the `uuid` of a calendar returned by `listCalendars`, or the `calendarUuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`.

get.description:
List the events of one calendar that overlap a time range. It covers one calendar only: get the calendars from `listCalendars` and call it for each. The range runs from `start` (inclusive) to `end` (exclusive), at most 32 days; for a longer period call it again with the next range. Recurring events are expanded: each occurrence is a separate item with the same `uuid` and its own `recurrenceId`. Results are not paginated.
Items hold summary fields only. For description, location, attendees and organizer call `getCalendarEvent` with the `calendarUuid`, `uuid` (as `eventUuid`) and `recurrenceId` of the item. Times are in UTC; `timeZone` is the zone the event was created in. `participationStatus` is the answer of the mailbox to an invitation from someone else, null for its own events. `status` CANCELLED means the organizer cancelled the event.

parameters.name: mailboxResourceId
parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the bearer token is authorized for.

parameters.name: calendarUuid
parameters.description: Calendar identifier: the `uuid` of a calendar returned by `listCalendars`, or the `calendarUuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start of the range, inclusive. ISO 8601 date-time with offset.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End of the range, exclusive. ISO 8601 date-time after `start` and at most 32 days after it.

parameters.name: timeZone
parameters.description: IANA time zone used to place all-day events and events without a time zone on days, also across a daylight saving change. Defaults to the fixed offset of `start`.

delete.description:
Delete an event, one occurrence of a recurring event, or a recurring event from one occurrence on. This cannot be undone. `calendarUuid` and `eventUuid` come from `listCalendarEvents`.
For a one-off event omit `scope` and `recurrenceId`. For a recurring event, `scope` `this` removes only the occurrence at `recurrenceId`, `future` removes it and every later one, `all` (the default) deletes the whole series.
An event with `editable` true can be deleted with any scope, and its attendees receive a cancellation or the updated series by email. An invitation from someone else on the own calendar of the mailbox can be deleted with `all` or `this`: the organizer receives a decline for the removed occurrences. Any other event is rejected with `403` and code `ERR_EVENT_NOT_EDITABLE`. `notifyAttendees` false deletes without sending any email.

parameters.name: mailboxResourceId
parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the bearer token is authorized for.

parameters.name: calendarUuid
parameters.description: Calendar identifier: the `uuid` of a calendar returned by `listCalendars`, or the `calendarUuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`.

parameters.name: eventUuid
parameters.description: Event identifier: the `uuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`. Every occurrence of a recurring event has the same uuid; `recurrenceId` picks one occurrence.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: For a recurring event: `this` removes the occurrence at `recurrenceId`, `future` removes it and every later one, `all` deletes the whole series. Omitted means `all`. Required when `recurrenceId` is sent.

parameters.name: recurrenceId
parameters.description: `recurrenceId` of one occurrence, copied unchanged from a `listCalendarEvents` item. Required when `scope` is `this` or `future`. A value that matches no occurrence, or any value on a one-off event, returns `404`.

parameters.name: notifyAttendees
parameters.description: `false` deletes without emailing attendees a cancellation or update, or the organizer a decline. Omitted means `true`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional `etag` from `getCalendarEvent`. When the event changed since that call, nothing is deleted and the request fails with `412`: fetch the event again and retry. Omit it to apply the request to the current version.

get.description:
Retrieve the full details of one event: title, times, description, location, meeting link, recurrence rule, reminder, organizer, attendees with their answers, and its `etag`. `calendarUuid` and `eventUuid` come from `listCalendarEvents` (the `calendarUuid` and `uuid` of an item). For one occurrence of a recurring event pass the `recurrenceId` of the item; without it the whole series is returned and `recurrenceId` is null. A `recurrenceId` that matches no occurrence returns `404`.
Call it before `updateCalendarEvent`, which replaces every field, so the values that should stay can be sent back. `replyable` true means the mailbox was invited by someone else and can answer with `replyToCalendarEvent`. `editable` true means the event can be changed or moved.

parameters.name: mailboxResourceId
parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the bearer token is authorized for.

parameters.name: calendarUuid
parameters.description: Calendar identifier: the `uuid` of a calendar returned by `listCalendars`, or the `calendarUuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`.

parameters.name: eventUuid
parameters.description: Event identifier: the `uuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`. Every occurrence of a recurring event has the same uuid; `recurrenceId` picks one occurrence.

parameters.name: recurrenceId
parameters.description: `recurrenceId` of one occurrence, copied unchanged from a `listCalendarEvents` item. Omit it for a one-off event or for the whole series.

put.description:
Change the details of an event: title, times, description, location, attendees, recurrence and so on. Every field replaces the stored value and an omitted optional field is cleared, so call `getCalendarEvent` first and send back the values that should stay. To only move an event in time, use `rescheduleCalendarEvent`. Only an event with `editable` true can be changed; any other is rejected with `403` and code `ERR_EVENT_NOT_EDITABLE`.
For a recurring event, `scope` `this` changes only the occurrence at `recurrenceId`, `future` ends the series before that occurrence and starts a new one with a new `uuid`, `all` (the default) changes the whole series, keeping the date of its first occurrence.
Attendees receive an email update, added attendees an invitation and removed ones a cancellation, unless `notifyAttendees` is false. Returns the changed event, or the changed occurrence for `scope` `this`.

parameters.name: mailboxResourceId
parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the bearer token is authorized for.

parameters.name: calendarUuid
parameters.description: Calendar identifier: the `uuid` of a calendar returned by `listCalendars`, or the `calendarUuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`.

parameters.name: eventUuid
parameters.description: Event identifier: the `uuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`. Every occurrence of a recurring event has the same uuid; `recurrenceId` picks one occurrence.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional `etag` from `getCalendarEvent`. When the event changed since that call, nothing is changed and the request fails with `412`: fetch the event again and retry. Omit it to apply the request to the current version.

post.description:
Answer an invitation from someone else: accept, decline or tentatively accept. It saves the answer on the event and emails it to the organizer, which cannot be recalled. `calendarUuid` and `eventUuid` come from `listCalendarEvents`.
It works only when `getCalendarEvent` returns `replyable` true. An event the mailbox organizes or is not invited to is rejected with `403` and code `ERR_EVENT_NOT_REPLYABLE`, an event the organizer cancelled with `409` and code `ERR_EVENT_CANCELLED`. Send the `recurrenceId` of an item to answer one occurrence of a recurring event, or omit it to answer the whole series. Returns the event with the new `participationStatus`.

parameters.name: mailboxResourceId
parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the bearer token is authorized for.

parameters.name: calendarUuid
parameters.description: Calendar identifier: the `uuid` of a calendar returned by `listCalendars`, or the `calendarUuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`.

parameters.name: eventUuid
parameters.description: Event identifier: the `uuid` of an event returned by `listCalendarEvents`. Every occurrence of a recurring event has the same uuid; `recurrenceId` picks one occurrence.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional `etag` from `getCalendarEvent`. When the event changed since that call, the answer is not saved and the request fails with `412`: fetch the event again and retry. Omit it to apply the request to the current version.

put.description:
Move an event to another time or change its length, keeping everything else (title, attendees, description and so on) as stored, so the event does not have to be fetched first. To change other fields use `updateCalendarEvent`. `calendarUuid` and `eventUuid` come from `listCalendarEvents`. Only an event with `editable` true can be moved; any other is rejected with `403` and code `ERR_EVENT_NOT_EDITABLE`.
For a recurring event, `scope` `this` moves only the occurrence at `recurrenceId`, `future` ends the series before that occurrence and starts a new one with a new `uuid`, `all` (the default) moves the whole series: only the time of day and the length apply and the series keeps the date of its first occurrence.
Attendees receive an email update unless `notifyAttendees` is false. Returns the moved event, or the moved occurrence for `scope` `this`.

post.description:
Send the user's feedback about the Hostinger Email API to the Hostinger mail team.

Only call this when the user explicitly asks to send feedback, report a problem, or request a feature. Send the user's own words; never include tokens, passwords or email contents. The message is capped at 2000 characters.

A `429` (`ERR_FEEDBACK_RATE_LIMIT`) means feedback for this customer was submitted less than ten seconds ago; wait and retry.

parameters.description: Resource ID of the managed mailbox the feedback is about, as returned by `GET /api/v1/me`.

V1.CalendarEvents.AttendeeInput.description: Person to invite to an event.

name.description: Display name of the attendee, null when unknown.

V1.CalendarEvents.Collection.description: Calendar events overlapping the requested time range. Not paginated.

truncated.description: Whether some events were left out because the calendar holds too many to list in one request.

V1.CalendarEvents.CreateRequest.description: Body for creating a calendar event.

start.description: ISO 8601 date-time with offset; without an offset it is read as UTC. For an all-day event a date is enough (2026-09-28).

end.description: Exclusive end, same format as `start`. Required for a timed event and not before `start`. For an all-day event the day after the last day (2026-09-29 for one day on 2026-09-28); omitted means one day.

allDay.description: `true` for an all-day event (dates only, `timeZone` ignored), `false` for an event at a time of day.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the event. Required when `allDay` is false, ignored when `allDay` is true.

description.description: Notes of the event. Omitted or null for none.

location.description: Place of the event. Omitted or null for none.

meetingLink.description: http or https URL of the online meeting. Omitted or null for none.

color.description: Color of the event as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. Omitted or null uses the calendar color.

recurrenceRule.description: Omitted or null for a one-off event. A repeating event sends every field of the rule, null when unused: `frequency` DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY or YEARLY, `interval` 1 to 1000, and `count` or `until` to end it, not both.

reminder.description: Alarm before the start: `value` 0 to 1000 and `unit`. Omitted or null for none.

attendees.description: People to invite; each receives an email invitation. Unique addresses, at most 100 not counting the mailbox itself, across all occurrences. The own address of the mailbox is stored as accepted and not invited. Omitted, null or empty for none.

V1.CalendarEvents.Event.description: Full details of one calendar event. Requested without `recurrenceId`, a recurring event is the series itself and `recurrenceId` is null; with it, one occurrence of the series.

etag.description: Version of the event. Send it as `If-Match` on a write to fail instead of overwriting a newer version.

replyable.description: Whether the mailbox is invited by someone else and the event is not cancelled, so `replyToCalendarEvent` can answer it.

recurrenceRule.description: How the event repeats. Null for a one-off event.

reminder.description: Alarm before the start. Null for none.

organizer.description: Who organizes the event. Null when the event has no organizer.

V1.CalendarEvents.EventListItem.description: Summary of one calendar event or of one occurrence of a recurring event.

uuid.description: Event identifier, the `eventUuid` of the calendar event endpoints. Every occurrence of a recurring event has the same uuid.

calendarUuid.description: Identifier of the calendar the event is stored in.

recurrenceId.description: Identifies one occurrence of a recurring event. Null for a one-off event or for the series itself.

start.description: Start in UTC. When `allDay` is true, the date at midnight (2026-09-29T00:00:00.000000Z). An event stored without a time zone keeps its wall-clock time (09:00 is 09:00:00.000000Z).

end.description: Exclusive end, same form as `start`. When `allDay` is true, midnight of the day after the last day of the event (2026-09-30T00:00:00.000000Z for a one-day event on 2026-09-29).

timeZone.description: IANA time zone the event is stored in. Null when it has none.

editable.description: Whether `updateCalendarEvent`, `rescheduleCalendarEvent` and `deleteCalendarEvent` can change the event.

color.description: Color of the event. The calendar color when the event has none or is an invitation from someone else.

participationStatus.description: Answer of the mailbox to an invitation from someone else. Null for its own events.

status.description: CANCELLED when the organizer cancelled the event, CONFIRMED otherwise.

V1.CalendarEvents.RecurrenceDay.description: One weekday of a recurrence rule.

position.description: Which such weekday in the month or year, for a MONTHLY or YEARLY rule only: 1 is the first, -1 the last, never 0. Null means every such weekday and is the only value allowed for other frequencies.

V1.CalendarEvents.RecurrenceRule.description: How an event repeats. Every field is always present, null when unused.

frequency.description: Unit of repetition. Only DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY and YEARLY can be written; SECONDLY, MINUTELY and HOURLY appear only on events created by other calendar applications.

interval.description: Repeat every this many units of `frequency`. 1 to 1000 when writing.

byDay.description: Weekdays the event repeats on. Null when unused.

byMonthDay.description: Days of the month, 1 to 31. Negative values count from the end of the month: -1 is the last day. Always null for a WEEKLY rule.

byMonth.description: Months, 1 is January. Null when unused.

count.description: Number of occurrences after which the series ends, at most 1000 when writing. Never set together with `until`.

until.description: Moment after which the series ends, not before the start of the event. Never set together with `count`.

weekStart.description: First day of the week used by the rule. Null when not set.

V1.CalendarEvents.Reminder.description: Alarm of an event: how long before the start it fires.

value.description: How many units before the start. 0 is at the start time. At most 1000 when writing.

recurrenceId.description: `recurrenceId` of one occurrence, copied unchanged from a `listCalendarEvents` item, to answer only that occurrence. Omitted or null answers the whole event.

V1.CalendarEvents.RescheduleRequest.description: Body for moving a calendar event to another time or changing its length.

start.description: ISO 8601 date-time with offset; without an offset it is read as UTC. For an all-day event a date is enough (2026-09-28).

end.description: Exclusive end, same format as `start`. Required for a timed event and not before `start`. For an all-day event the day after the last day (2026-09-29 for one day on 2026-09-28); omitted means one day.

allDay.description: `true` for an all-day event (dates only, `timeZone` ignored), `false` for an event at a time of day.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the event. Required when `allDay` is false, ignored when `allDay` is true.

scope.description: For a recurring event: `this` moves the occurrence at `recurrenceId`, `future` moves it and every later one, `all` moves the whole series. Omitted or null means `all`. Required when `recurrenceId` is sent.

recurrenceId.description: `recurrenceId` of one occurrence, copied unchanged from a `listCalendarEvents` item. Required when `scope` is `this` or `future`, ignored for `all`.

notifyAttendees.description: `false` saves the change without emailing attendees, and copies of the event in the calendars of other Hostinger mailboxes are not updated. Omitted or null means `true`.

x-mcp-instructions:
Hostinger Mail API access - use this server when the user wants to read, search, send, organize, or manage email in their Hostinger mailbox(es), manage email webhooks, or work with the calendars and calendar events of a mailbox.

Capabilities:
- List mailboxes belonging to the authenticated Hostinger order
- List folders inside a mailbox (Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Trash, custom)
- List, search, fetch, move, delete, flag messages
- Read message body (text/HTML), full RFC822 source, attachments
- Send email from a mailbox
- Manage webhooks (create, list, test, regenerate secret, delete)
- Manage calendars of a mailbox (list, create, update, delete)
- List, read, create, update, reschedule and delete calendar events, and answer invitations
- Send the user's feedback about this API to the Hostinger mail team (`POST /api/v1/mailboxes/{mailboxResourceId}/feedback`)

Mailbox discovery: there is no standalone "list mailboxes" endpoint. Call `GET /api/v1/me` first — the response contains `data.mailboxes[]` with each mailbox's `resourceId` and `address`. Use that `resourceId` as `mailboxResourceId` in every other endpoint.

Every operation is exposed as its own tool; use only the tools that are listed. Path templates use `{placeholder}` substitution.

Calendars: call `listCalendars` first to get the `calendarUuid` every calendar event operation needs; use the calendar with `default` true unless the user names another one. `listCalendarEvents` covers one calendar and at most 32 days per call. `updateCalendarEvent` replaces every field, so call `getCalendarEvent` first and send back the values the user did not ask to change; to only move an event use `rescheduleCalendarEvent`. Creating, changing or deleting an event with attendees and answering an invitation send emails that cannot be recalled - confirm with the user first. Calendar endpoints return `403` with code `ERR_PAYWALL` when the mailbox plan does not include the calendar.

Auth: each request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <customer-Hostinger-token>`. Tokens are scoped to one Hostinger order and may be further restricted to specific mailboxes within that order — assume access is partial unless verified.

Feedback: only call `POST /api/v1/mailboxes/{mailboxResourceId}/feedback` when the user explicitly asks to send feedback, report a problem, or request a feature. Send the user's own words, keep it under 2000 characters, and never include tokens, passwords or email contents.
